DwG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http: //www.dilg.com.ph DILG OPINION No. 85 s. 2022 AUG 26 2022 DIR. LEOCADIO T. TROVELA, CESO Ill Regional Director, DILG Region VII Sudlon, Lahug, Cebu City Dear RD Trovela: This has reference to your letter of indorsement dated 08 August 2022 referring to the Central Office the letter from Ms. Farah Diba G. Gentuya, Director, DILG-Negros Oriental. In her e-mail dated August 3, 2022, PD Gentuya is requesting guidance or opinion on whether or not the Execom of the Provincial Development Council can conduct official business even without the reorganization of the full council considering that CSOs have no holdover capacity and there are newly-elected Mayors in Negros Oriental. At the outset, we deem it proper to highlight Section 106 of Republic Act No. 7160 otherwise known as the "Local Government Code of 1991" (LGC), which provides that each local government unit (LGU) shall have a comprehensive multi-sectoral development plan to be initiated by the Local Development Council (LDC) concerned and approved by its sanggunian. Accordingly, under Section 107 of the LGC, the provincial development council shall be headed by the governor and shall be composed of all mayors of component cities and municipalities, chairman of the committee on appropriations of the sangguniang panlalawigan, the congressman or his representative, and representatives of non- governmental organizations operating in the province, who shall constitute not less than one-fourth (h) of the members of the fully organized council. Moreover, pursuant to Rule XIII, Article 64 of the Implementing Rules and Regulations (IRR) of the LGC, the sanggunian shall complete the accreditation process of people's organizations (POs), non-governmental organizations (NGOs) or the Private Sector within sixty days (60) days from the promulgation of said rules or within the same period from the organization of the newly-elected Sangunian, and within fifteen (15) days after the accreditation process, the DILG Field Officer assigned in the LGU shall call all, POs, NGOs, or private sector to a meeting where these organizations shall choose from among themselves which organizations will be represented in the local special bodies, which include among others, the Provincial Development Council (PDC). Correspondingly, the same IRR provides that the term of office of a selected representative of the people's organization, NGOs, or private sector shall be "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

coterminous with that of the local chief executive concerned. Relatedly, this Department issued Memorandum Circular No. 2022-831, dated 15 June 2022, which states that within the 2nd week of September, duly authorized representatives of all accredited Civil Society Organizations (CSOs) shall hold a meeting where such groups shall choose from among themselves the representative- organizations to the local special bodies, which include among others, the PDC. Notably, under Section III of the LGC, it is provided that each local development council shall create an executive committee to represent it and act in its behalf when it is not in session, and the executive committee of the provincial development council shall be composed of the governor as chairman, the representative of component city and municipal mayors to be chosen from among themselves, the chairman of the committee on appropriations of the sangguniang panlalawigan, the president of the provincial league of barangays, and a representative of non-governmental organizations that are represented in the council, as members. In •view thereof, considering that the term of office of a selected representative shall be coterminous with that of the local chief executive concerned, we are of the view that it is imperative that a reorganization of the composition of the LDC, which includes the determination of the CSO representative to the LDC, must precede before the LDC and the Executive Committee can fully convene and conduct official business, taking into account the functions of the LDC which is to assist the corresponding sanggunian in setting the direction of economic, and social development, and coordinating development efforts within its territorial jurisdiction. Hence, before the LDC and the Executive Committee can function and conduct official business, the determination of CSO representative to the LDC must first be determined and ascertained, in order to ensure the pathways to bring collective interests and voicing the people's concerns at the local development planning. This opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the courts. We hope to have assisted you accordingly. Thank you. Very truly yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: GAN MAR Undersec ary for Local Governme OUSLG/ML1/LLLS-LRALLD,tjwclp COPY FURNISHED: FARAH DIBA G.
